answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a mirror as the anchor of the cost.
